hello.note: The classic greeting: السلام عليكم (as-salamu 'alaykum); reply وعليكم السلام (wa 'alaykum as-salam).

goodbye.note: Also: إلى اللقاء (ila al-liqa), literally 'until the meeting'.

please.note: To a woman: min fadliki (same spelling). In casual speech often min fadlak.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: شكرا جزيلا (shukran jazilan).

youre_welcome.note: Also: لا شكر على واجب (la shukra 'ala wajib), 'no thanks needed for a duty'.

sorry.note: A woman says: آسفة (asifa). Also: عذرا ('udhran).

excuse_me.note: To a woman: law samahti (same spelling).

good_morning.note: The reply: صباح النور (sabah an-nur), 'morning of light'.

how_are_you.note: To a woman: kayfa haluki? (same spelling). Also: كيف الحال؟ (kayfa al-hal?)

im_fine.note: Very often answered with الحمد لله (al-hamdu lillah), 'thank God'.

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: ma ismuki? (same spelling).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also: فرصة سعيدة (fursa sa'ida), 'a happy occasion'.

where_from.note: To a woman: min ayna anti? (same spelling).

speak_english.note: To a woman: هل تتكلمين الإنجليزية؟ (hal tatakallamin al-injiliziyya?)

dont_understand.note: Also: لم أفهم (lam afham), 'I didn't understand'.

speak_slowly.note: To a woman: تكلمي ببطء من فضلك (takallami bibut min fadliki).

what.note: Before a noun use ما (ma): ما هذا؟ (ma hadha?), 'what is this?'

who.note: Usually written without the vowel mark, so it looks like من (min, 'from'); context tells them apart.

how_much.note: For a feminine item: بكم هذه؟ (bikam hadhihi?)

where_bathroom.note: Also very common: أين الحمام؟ (ayna al-hammam?)

can_you_help.note: To a woman: hal yumkinuki musa'adati? (same spelling).

what_means.note: Also: ماذا يعني هذا؟ (madha ya'ni hadha?)

two.note: Arabic digit: ٢. Also heard as اثنين (ithnayn).

four.note: Arabic digit: ٤. The ' marks ayn, a sound squeezed from deep in the throat.

five.note: Arabic digit: ٥. kh as in Scottish 'loch'.

six.note: Arabic digit: ٦. Hold the double t: sit-ta.

water.note: Long a with a light catch at the end. Bottled water: مياه معدنية (miyah ma'daniyya).

im_hungry.note: A woman says: أنا جائعة (ana jai'a). In speech also جوعان (ju'an).

menu_please.note: To a woman: min fadliki. In restaurants you will also hear المنيو (al-minyu).

bill_please.note: To a woman: min fadliki (same spelling).

delicious.note: For a feminine noun, e.g. الوجبة (the meal): لذيذة (ladhidha).

no_meat.note: Also: أنا نباتي (ana nabati), 'I'm vegetarian'; a woman says نباتية (nabatiyya).

left.note: To the left: إلى اليسار (ila al-yasar).

right.note: To the right: إلى اليمين (ila al-yamin).

straight_ahead.note: In everyday speech many say على طول ('ala tul).

stop_here.note: To a woman: توقفي هنا من فضلك (tawaqqafi huna min fadliki).

is_it_far.note: For a feminine place, e.g. المحطة (the station): هل هي بعيدة؟ (hal hiya ba'ida?)

one_ticket.note: To a woman: min fadliki. Return ticket: تذكرة ذهاب وعودة (tadhkirat dhahab wa 'awda).

too_expensive.note: Also: السعر مرتفع جدا (as-si'r murtafi' jiddan), 'the price is very high'.

id_like_this.note: To a woman: min fadliki. For a feminine item say هذه (hadhihi) instead of هذا.

pay_card.note: Also: هل تقبلون البطاقات؟ (hal taqbalun al-bitaqat?), 'do you accept cards?'

cash.note: I'll pay in cash: سأدفع نقدا (sa-adfa' naqdan). In speech often كاش (kash).

tomorrow.note: Careful: غداء (ghada), with a long a, means lunch.

good_night.note: To a woman: تصبحين على خير (tusbihin 'ala khayr). Also: ليلة سعيدة (layla sa'ida).

see_you_later.note: To a woman: araki lahiqan (same spelling).

wait_moment.note: To a woman: انتظري لحظة من فضلك (intadhiri lahdha min fadliki). Short: لحظة (lahdha).

call_police.note: Said to everyone around. To one man: اتصل (ittasil); to one woman: اتصلي (ittasili).

im_lost.note: Also: أنا تائه (ana taih); a woman says تائهة (taiha).

dont_feel_well.note: Also: أنا مريض (ana marid), 'I'm ill'; a woman says مريضة (marida).

lost_phone.note: In everyday speech a phone is often جوال (jawwal) or موبايل (mobayl).

allergic.note: Also: عندي حساسية من … ('indi hassasiyya min …).

be_careful.note: To a woman: انتبهي! (intabihi!) To a group: انتبهوا! (intabihu!)

no_problem.note: Also: لا بأس (la bas), 'it's all right'.

dont_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: لا تعجبني (la tu'jibuni).

im_tired.note: A woman says: أنا متعبة (ana mut'aba).

im_happy.note: A woman says: أنا سعيدة (ana sa'ida).

welcome.note: The reply: أهلا بك (ahlan bika); to a woman, ahlan biki.

congratulations.note: Reply: بارك الله فيك (barak allah fika; to a woman, fiki). More formal: تهانينا! (tahanina!)
